name: Broadford Lake Park
blurb: Oakland's lake park and the biggest municipal park in the county. A swimming beach, boat launch, and boat and pavilion rentals, with picnic ground, volleyball and basketball behind it.

restrooms.note: Reported first-hand. Whether they stay open outside the beach season is the part that matters and is not confirmed.

hoursNote: Seasonal. The beach and much of the park close outside summer — confirm before driving out in spring or autumn.

fee.note: Pavilions and boats can be rented, per the Chamber's listing. Whether there is an entry or beach fee, and how much, is not confirmed — the Town of Oakland sets it and its website is currently unreachable.

sources.label: Garrett County Chamber of Commerce: Broadford Lake Park
Garrett County Chamber of Commerce: Broadford Lake Park listing
sources.note: Confirms the lake, beach area, volleyball, basketball, boat launch, and boat and pavilion rentals. Mentions neither fees, restrooms nor a playground.

outstanding: PRIORITY: get the entry fee and season-pass prices from the Town of Oakland directly. Figures circulate online but the town's own site is unreachable and we will not publish a number we cannot read at source.
Confirm the season the beach is open and staffed, and whether the park is accessible outside it.
Confirm whether the restrooms stay open outside the beach season.
Confirm boat rental prices and what is available to rent.

corrections.was: "Believed to charge an entry or beach fee in season."
corrections.now: We don't know, and "believed" is not something this site is allowed to publish. It was a guess with no source behind it, which is the one thing every page here promises not to do. The fee is now marked unconfirmed until the Town of Oakland confirms it.

reports.what: There are restrooms, a playground and a beach area.
Playground, lake area, restrooms, trails and pavilions.

name: Town Park East
blurb: The larger of Accident's two town parks, on the southern end of South Street. A full playground, a little league field, a quarter-mile walking loop, horseshoe pits and a tennis court. A genuine neighborhood park rather than a scenic one.

fee.note: Not confirmed. Most town parks here are free to enter, but nobody has checked this one.

sources.label: Town of Accident: community
sources.note: Park facilities as listed by the town.

outstanding: RESTROOMS — confirm.
Confirm the walking loop surface — a quarter mile is useful for a stroller or a wheelchair only if it's paved.
Confirm it is free and has no gate hours.
Get the Town of Accident number.

name: Town Park West
blurb: The smaller Accident park, at the western end of Wood Street. A large pavilion plus climbing cubes, a saucer swing, a seesaw, and a swing set with an accessible seat. That last one is worth knowing. Accessible play equipment is rare out here and almost never published.

restrooms.note: Reported first-hand. Whether they are open year-round is not confirmed.

accessibility: Swing set includes a handicap accessible seat, per the town's own listing.

fee.note: Free to use the park. The pavilion can be booked and there is a charge for that — the amount is not confirmed.

sources.label: Town of Accident: community
sources.note: Pavilion and playground equipment, including the accessible swing seat.

outstanding: Get the pavilion rental charge and how to book it from the Town of Accident.
Confirm whether the restrooms are open year-round.
Confirm park hours.

reports.what: Restrooms, and a pavilion you can rent. No charge to use the park itself; the pavilion rental is charged.

name: Friendsville Community Park
blurb: The town's park on the Youghiogheny, with a paved walking and biking loop, a river access ramp and a small sand beach. Two baseball fields, basketball, tennis, sand volleyball and horseshoe pits, a large playground and a lot of open ground.

restrooms.note: Reported first-hand. Whether they are permanent or seasonal, and their hours, are not confirmed.

fee.note: Not confirmed. Most town parks here are free to enter, but nobody has checked this one.

warnings: River access here is on serious whitewater. The Youghiogheny through Friendsville is not a place to swim casually.

sources.label: Town of Friendsville: Riverside Community Park
sources.note: Facilities as listed by the town.

sources.label: Garrett County Chamber of Commerce: Town of Friendsville
sources.note: Lists the park's facilities in full: paved loop, river access ramp, small sand beach, fishing on Bear Creek and the Youghiogheny, two baseball fields, pavilions, basketball, horseshoe pits, sand volleyball, tennis, large playground. Mentions neither restrooms nor pickleball.

outstanding: Confirm whether the tennis courts are lined for pickleball, or whether there are dedicated pickleball courts. Reported first-hand; the town's own facilities listing mentions tennis but not pickleball.
Confirm whether the restrooms are permanent or seasonal, and their hours.
Confirm whether the sand beach is a swimming beach or river access only — the listing says beach but never says swimming.
Confirm park hours and whether the paved loop is lit.

corrections.was: That there is no beach here.
corrections.now: There is a small sand beach. The Chamber's own listing for the town says so, and we had it as a flat no — which is worse than leaving it blank, because a flat no stops the park appearing when someone searches for one. Whether it is a swimming beach or river access only is still not confirmed.

reports.what: There are restrooms, a play area, ball fields and pickleball.

fieldNotes.author: Matt
fieldNotes.body: Restrooms, a play area and ball fields. There is pickleball here too, though the town's own listing only mentions tennis, so I do not know yet whether it is dedicated courts or lines painted on the tennis.

name: Maryland 4-H Environmental Education & Camping Center
address: 1916 Maryland Highway, Suite A, Mountain Lake Park, MD 21550
blurb: Long known locally as Pleasant Valley. Over 1,100 acres run by University of Maryland Extension, part open to anyone and part reserved for camp programs and private hires. The swimming beach, boating, challenge course, archery and shooting range and the cabins all sit on the reserved side.

restrooms.note: Extension lists modern bath houses. Those are on the reserved side — whether anything is open to a public visitor is not confirmed.

hoursNote: Lake and beach reported open daily in summer. Season dates unconfirmed.

fee.note: Not confirmed for public use. Facility hire is priced separately by Extension.

warnings: This is a working camp, not a public park. The beach, boats, ranges and cabins are for camp programs and booked groups.
Confirm with the center before planning a visit around anything beyond the lake, trails and fishing.

sources.label: University of Maryland Extension: Maryland 4-H Environmental Education & Camping Center
sources.note: The operator. Gives the proper name, over 1,100 acres, the address and phone, and splits what the public may use from what sits on the private side.

sources.label: University of Maryland Extension: private events
sources.note: States the facility is open to the public for reservations, and names the booking contact.

outstanding: Confirm what a member of the public can actually reach without a booking — is the lake shore walkable, and from where?
Confirm whether there is any public restroom, as distinct from the camp bath houses.
Confirm whether fishing needs a permit or prior notice.
Confirm facility hire rates and minimum group size.
access: Two halves. Extension says the public gets the lake, hiking trails, fishing, biking and wildlife viewing. Swimming, boating, shooting sports, the challenge course, sports fields, bath houses and cabins are listed under the private side — available through a camp program or by booking the facility, not by turning up. Bookings and questions: 301-334-6960.

corrections.was: "Thirteen hundred acres run by the University of Maryland, with a lake and beach open daily through the summer for swimming, fishing and canoeing." Swimming and the beach were listed as available.
corrections.now: It is over 1,100 acres, and Extension — the operator — puts swimming, boating, the ranges, the challenge course and the cabins on the PRIVATE side, available through a camp program or by booking. Only the lake, trails, fishing, biking and wildlife viewing are described as public. Our version would have sent a family there to swim. It also came from a county tourism site rather than from Extension, which is the kind of source this site is not supposed to use at all — that is the root of it.

reports.what: Twelve rustic cabins for campers, an athletic field, a challenge course, a basketball, volleyball and four-square court, a beach area at the lake for swimming and canoeing, and marksmanship and archery ranges.

name: Grantsville Town Park
blurb: The town park in the middle of Grantsville, a block from the library and the restaurants. Playground, tennis and pickleball, basketball and sand volleyball, a softball diamond, and pavilions you can book.

restrooms.note: Reported first-hand. Whether they stay open through the winter is not confirmed.

fee.note: No charge reported for the park itself. Pavilions can be booked and are charged; the amount is not confirmed.

restrooms.note: Reported first-hand. Season and hours not confirmed.

blurb: A boardwalk trail through wetland rather than a park with a field in it. Restrooms are on site, though not always unlocked. Worth planning around rather than counting on.

restrooms.note: On site, but reported as sometimes locked. Nobody has established when they are open, so treat them as a maybe rather than a yes.
